page.title: Digital work sized to the actual problem.
page.lede: The goal is not to introduce the most technology. It is to build or improve a system that is useful, maintainable, appropriately secure, and clearly owned.

items.name: Websites
items.description: Lightweight, accessible business websites with maintainable source, sensible hosting, and clear ownership.

items.name: Custom Applications
items.description: Focused web or offline applications shaped around the workflow instead of forcing the workflow around a product.

items.name: Workflow Automation
items.description: Practical automation for repetitive processes, handoffs, document movement, and system-to-system tasks when justified.

items.name: Technical Consulting
items.description: Architecture, troubleshooting, technical planning, platform choices, and practical problem-solving without unnecessary product sales.

items.name: Digital Asset Ownership & Vendor Transitions
items.description: Inventory and transition domains, DNS, hosting, repositories, cloud accounts, business profiles, and administrator access so critical assets are controlled by the business and outside providers use named, appropriately scoped access.
examples: Domain, DNS, hosting, and repository transitions
Named or delegated vendor access and least-privilege cleanup
Vendor offboarding, handoff, and recovery documentation
Secure credential-sharing setup when delegated access is not available

items.name: Maintenance & Improvement
items.description: Ongoing fixes, accessibility and performance improvements, dependency updates, documentation, and measured modernization.

startingPoints.title: Build something new
startingPoints.description: Start from a clear business need and choose the smallest maintainable architecture that solves it.

startingPoints.title: Improve what already exists
startingPoints.description: Keep the useful parts, identify the friction, and modernize only where the change earns its cost.

startingPoints.title: Untangle ownership, access, or a vendor transition
startingPoints.description: Inventory the current assets and administrators, move critical accounts toward business-controlled ownership, remove obsolete access, verify MFA and recovery responsibility, and document the handoff.

platformNote.title: Not every project needs a platform.
platformNote.body: Static hosting, open formats, portable repositories, and low recurring costs are preferred when they meet the requirement. Databases, authentication services, paid SaaS, or other infrastructure should earn their place.
